Every packet may publish prelaunch-resource-refusal only when its raw observation matches exactly one registered free-space, projected-storage, or projected-process-hours refusal condition; solverLaunched is false. Only c0v-radial-produce additionally permits preproduction-artifact-refusal from the sole clean-worktree-materializable filesystem-object-policy condition.

All three resource truth values are rederived for every receipt. PASS requires all three true; resource refusal requires exactly one false and the selected condition ID; radial artifact refusal requires all three resource conditions true plus exactly one selected science/reference live-binding failure while every other binding remains exact.

The process projection uses exact integers: projectedPackageElapsedNanosecondsAfterAttempt equals packageElapsedNanosecondsBeforeAttempt plus currentPacketRegisteredElapsedNanosecondsMaximum. Equality to packageElapsedNanosecondsMaximum 86400000000000 passes and one nanosecond greater refuses; process-hour fields equal their integer operands divided by 3600000000000 and never select a route independently.

On radial artifact refusal, observed.ancestry.boundArtifactsMatch true means every bound content identity, including the selected operand, exactly matches packet and launch-HEAD bytes; every other binding passes; and the sole selected failure is only the independently recorded regular-file single-link/unaliased-parent policy. Missing, mismatched, noncanonical, unreadable, outside-root, or Git-cleanliness-indeterminate operands fail-stop without a receipt.

The selected filesystem failure is safe to observe: its resolved target is proven inside the physical repository before opening, bytes are hashed through one descriptor, and canonical fstat device/file identity, size, and link count are identical before and after hashing. No outside-root alias is read.
Refusal evidence is an exact condition-specific authority/inline roster and cannot cite the enclosing preflight receipt or another cyclic current artifact.

The observer and writer require the exact parent watchdog issued with the same active run locks and locked catalogue/protocol authority. They synchronously recheck the live parent-monotonic clock at entry, after canonical derivation, immediately before registered staged publication, and after the exact final bytes are reopened; a caller-built, cross-action, or expired watchdog rejects and leaves any late installed receipt ignored behind stale locks.

The catalogue's 33554432-byte worker-message line limit is only a framing ceiling. Every packet row fixes maximumStdoutBytes at the 4194304-byte aggregate retained-stdout ceiling plus exact lifecycle, boundary/progress, artifact, and result line maxima/counts whose derived sum is no greater than that ceiling.

Every packet projectedScratchBytes exactly equals catalogue maximumStdoutBytes plus workerTransportContract.maximumStderrBytes plus catalogue maximumOtherAttemptRootBytes. The latter excludes stdout/stderr and is enforced by the terminal physical census over every other attempt-root path. Equality is allowed; one further byte in any class is infrastructure fail-stop and cannot become route or evidence authority.

The catalogue runtimeLauncherContract is design-frozen-source-absent: launcher source, executable identity, compiler/build contract, packet command rewrites, and run authority remain absent. Its exact Node/Git host identities, clean environment, physical cwd, sixteen packet-order check/run argv vectors, authenticated-channel message union, monotonic timeout, and bounded proxy are prospective authority only until all missing build operands resolve together. The parent now materializes only the exact nine-row catalogue clean environment for the worker, and the worker independently requires its complete environment to equal that roster; no ambient value is cloned.

A static launcher environment marker never proves provenance. Every packet protocol carries an exact launcherBoundaryContract: check is initial-auth then release; each run subroute is initial auth, preflight stage/install, direct terminal-candidate publication, selected path-ordered output stage/install pairs, optional verification stage/install, terminal stage/install, path-bound packet/package cleanup, and release last. Every request uses a fresh sequence-bound 32-byte challenge. The native launcher accepts success only after one complete exact roster; failure may retain only a strict non-release prefix and can never release executor output.

The inherited launcher-to-Node response read end is OS-nonblocking before child creation: Win32 uses CreatePipe and a checked SetNamedPipeHandleState PIPE_NOWAIT on the read handle before CreateProcess; POSIX uses a checked fcntl O_NONBLOCK before exec. Node polls with parent-owned hrtime; only EAGAIN or EWOULDBLOCK means no bytes, zero means EOF, and every other read error fail-stops.

Before every request, queued unsolicited bytes or EOF reject. After a canonical nonrelease response, Node drains the currently queued response bytes and rejects any nonempty drain or EOF; bytes arriving later reject at the next pre-request boundary. Release succeeds only after the canonical response followed by exact EOF with no intervening byte. Response and EOF share the same request-write-to-completion deadline.

Every launcher authentication interval uses an exact 30000 ms maximum: launcher-monotonic successful child creation to complete initial request, and Node parent-hrtime complete request write to complete response for nonrelease or complete response plus exact EOF for release. Equality passes and one millisecond greater fail-stops. Control frames are at most 4096 bytes; after release the launcher uses one fixed 65536-byte read/write buffer, drains before its next read, and never accumulates aggregate output.

The launcher never embeds or compares its own final executable SHA-256. It self-opens its canonical image before child creation and every response, requires those observations equal, and reports the current identity; Node independently reopens and hashes the resolved catalogue path on every response. Fresh private-pipe challenges, exact process.ppid, and a still-live launcher parent bind each publication/cleanup boundary without relying on PID existence alone. Direct Node invocation or channel/PID/image/peer/sequence/order drift cannot authorize an S6 run or claim.

Any preflight failure outside those exact registered conditions fail-stops before a terminal candidate, attempt row, ledger, packet verification, or final terminal receipt. It retains only the ignored raw attempt root and stale locks for review, cannot be relabeled as resource/scientific refusal, earns no packet or dependency completion credit, and requires a separately frozen successor protocol.
A passing observation cannot be relabeled as refusal, and a refusal receipt cannot substitute PASS-shaped observed values. Exit code never selects either route.

The independent cause evaluator reopens raw receipt bytes and live Git/manifest/resource facts; the later attempt-v2 classificationValidation embeds artifact-derived observations so ignored staging is corroboration only.

No earlier artifact contains this final receipt identity and no hash fixed point or placeholder is permitted.

Moving/static route-cause caps and nonproduce prelaunch/cap outcomes write and pin this receipt as maker-return evidence, write no phase10-packet-verification-v2 receipt, grant no packet/dependency credit, and require a successor protocol.

Every claim-bearing publication is bracketed by synchronous assertions on the exact parent watchdog bound to the active run locks and locked authority. The outer deadline includes final semantic revalidation and lock-cleanup eligibility decisions; physical unlink is non-claim cleanup, and a post-packet-unlink overrun retains the package lock and invalidates any already installed receipt.
The receipt never treats process exit alone as a cause and cannot inherit a worker verdict. The independent verifier reopens protocol, raw timing, preflight, resource census, and callable artifacts.

Unclassified crash, transport loss, negative-control invalidity, or census/resource/receipt infrastructure failure stops before terminalCandidate and therefore before attempt ledger, packet verification, and this final receipt. Only the ignored raw attempt root and stale locks remain for review; a separately frozen successor protocol with a new unique attempt ID is required.

No-worker rows have null exitCode and null raw signal. A started child has exactly one raw exitCode or signal in the governed exit-status artifact; the attempt-row exitCode is null for a signaled child and no mapped or fabricated code is allowed.
invariants: production-complete has terminalStatus pass or fail solely from the independent numerical evaluator; its classificationValidation is null.
Each of the five registered scientific refusal dispositions has terminalStatus refusal and a passing, empty-error independent classificationValidation.

No unclassified infrastructure or negative-control-invalid row is serializable under this schema. Such execution stops before terminalCandidate and retains only ignored raw state and stale locks until a separately frozen successor protocol audits it.

Every serialized row binds terminal-success-candidate.json. The final terminal-v2 receipt later binds this candidate plus the finalized ledger and the route-applicable verification-v2 in one direction.
branch remains the pinned S5 science branch even for reference-discrepancy-refusal; dispositionCode alone records the lifecycle route.
Every packet protocol freezes a finite exact executionRecord count tuple roster keyed by dispositionCode and terminalStatus; rows outside that roster reject.

Every packet protocol freezes one exact worker-leaf science/control invocation roster per execution tuple in route order. Completed scientific rows contain the full roster; registered-cap rows contain the exact prefix ending in the sole capped leaf. Missing, reordered, duplicate, extra, infrastructure-state, or falsely relabeled worker rows reject. Check callers are counted separately and never add overlapping timing rows around their evaluator/control children.

Freeze preflight and post-worker attempt-census/resource evaluators are acyclic verification stages outside executableInvocationRecords: their counters remain durable, but they never claim to validate their own later finish times or identities. Their overhead is excluded from processHours. Every governed worker executable leaf, including route-cause, is included and summed across every materialized attempt for the 24 process-hour package cap.

The radial solver-production invocation has the tighter S5 300-second worker cap. Every other registered executable control invocation has the foundation four-hour cap independently checked from its own timing row; no whole-attempt four-hour scientific cap exists.

Invocation cap classification is disjoint: complete rows are at or below their registered 300/14400-second maximum, while registered-cap rows are strictly above it. Equality is allowed for normal completion and never classifies registered-cap; raw infrastructure timing remains ignored and cannot enter this schema.

The parent-owned worker-progress file is retained staging, but its exact records are embedded in the tracked attempt row and compact-JSONL reserialization must reproduce the recorded artifact identity. Publication and later verification rederive registered-cap partialExecution solely from the embedded records and packet protocol.

The radial production-complete tuple is 1 protocol reopen, 1 reference reopen, 1 worker process, 1 solver worker, 1 production invocation, 0 discrepancy/refusal evaluators, 1 freeze evaluator, 1 resource evaluator, 1 attempt-census evaluator, 4 distinct check callers, 1 numerical evaluator, 3 numerical controls, 1 accepted valid witness, and 1 accepted numerical verdict.

The five radial registered-cap tuple families all have 1 protocol reopen, 1 reference reopen, 1 worker process, 1 solver worker, 1 production invocation, 1 post-worker cap-cause evaluator, 1 freeze evaluator, 1 resource evaluator, 1 attempt-census evaluator, and zero accepted witness/verdict counts. The production-cap family has 4 distinct check callers and numerical evaluator/control invocation-prefix counts 0/0. The evaluator-cap and three control-cap families have 5 distinct check callers because the radial science caller was entered before the capped leaf; their invocation-prefix numerical evaluator/control counts, including the sole capped leaf, are respectively 1/0, 1/1, 1/2, and 1/3. Every radial cap route has an empty executedNegativeControlIds roster and earns zero completed negative-control credit; earlier completed controls remain raw retained prefix facts only.

The current moving discrepancy and static preimplementation tuples are 1 protocol reopen, 1 reference/refusal reopen, 1 non-solver worker process, 0 solver/production invocations, 1 route-specific discrepancy/refusal evaluator, 1 freeze evaluator, 1 resource evaluator, 1 attempt-census evaluator, 4 distinct check callers, and zero numerical evaluator, numerical control, accepted witness, and accepted numerical verdict counts.

The moving/static route-cause cap tuples preserve the entered registered produce check-caller as a child-registered-cap caller result, have exactly 5 check-caller invocations, and grant no route-validity, packet-verification, result, or dependency credit. The route evaluator is invoked only as that caller's child and is never executed a second time for caller credit.

A late negative-control, census, resource, or receipt infrastructure failure cannot serialize a row, even when ignored candidate bytes or completed leaf timing exist. It retains the ignored root and stale locks only and earns zero accepted credit.

Freeze ancestry, final resource accounting, structural attempt census, and route-specific science/refusal validity remain separately owned and independently rederived; no caller-supplied lifecycle context can satisfy more than its registered check.
A registered-cap partialExecution binds the exact protocol cap, roster-prefix progress, capped-invocation time, executionRecord, and resource counts; non-prefix progress rejects.

Radial registered-cap authority enumerates exactly five cap positions: solver production at 300 seconds, numerical evaluator at 14400 seconds, and each of the three numerical negative-control leaves at 14400 seconds. The partial identifies the sole registered-cap invocation and later-leaf caps retain every earlier completed invocation/progress record while all accepted-credit counts remain zero.
The packet protocol freezes scratch observation points; deleting or superseding an intermediate file cannot reduce scratchBytes below the maximum already observed.

Package storage accounting counts each physical path copy without content deduplication. Before S6 it reopens the exact 12-file baseline: nine ignored S5 reference-root files totaling 1085192 bytes plus three separately tracked pinned S5 C0V outputs totaling 544385 bytes, for 1629577 bytes. Every preflight rederives that roster and all later retained copies before applying the 64 GiB cap.

resourceRecord is mandatory on every row; its point IDs and observations exactly match the selected route protocol, artifacts are path-sorted unique, concurrent byte sums rederive, timestamps are ordered within the attempt, maximumObservedConcurrentBytes equals scratchBytes, terminalRetainedBytes equals retainedBytes, and excludedLedgerPath is absent from every observation.

For a valid scientific classification, every observation cites at least one tracked-authority or tracked-evidence row regardless of conditionPassed. Ignored-staging evidence may corroborate but may never be its sole support.
Exit status alone never classifies production failure, resource refusal, or scientific refusal.

invariants: The independent verifier reopens every witness artifact and computes every check/negative-control verdict; a producer cannot supply either side of a comparison it participates in.

Supplemental A-P executes its governed leaves exactly once in protocol order: missing-producer control, uncalled-check control, artifact-index producer, then the registered check-caller wrapper, which invokes the independent evaluator exactly once. Each control callable owns its retained phase10-ap-negative-control-v1 output; the index producer only assembles those existing bytes. The evaluator and final verifier reopen each receipt's complete baseline/mutated registry projections, canonical-reserialize and hash them, independently derive the exact named mutation, rerun the registered owner check, and exact-compare the refusal before granting control credit.

Publish packets execute producer then registered check-caller wrapper; aggregate executes its any-layer-nonpass control, producer, then registered check-caller wrapper. A wrapper invokes its independent evaluator exactly once, and candidate/check credit comes only from the returned caller result rather than a protocol-copied roster.

The aggregate control retains one canonical definitions.aggregateAnyLayerNonpassControl receipt at the exact strict-preflight observed.attemptDirectory/any-layer-nonpass-control.json path before the aggregate producer runs. The packet attemptRoot parent without the registered attempt ID is forbidden. The producer embeds only its strict negativeControlResult; the aggregate check-caller and final verifier independently rederive the exact one-field radial mutation and both clean/attacked outcomes from the full retained receipt.

The published phase10-c0v-terminal-table-v1 has tableId c0v-terminal-table-v1 and exactly three definitions.aggregateTerminalTableRow rows in radial, static, moving order. Every row is rederived from its exact committed result identity; no copied disposition can disagree with those bytes.

It is the complete produce-attempt ledger for this one-protocol/one-attempt v1 history, not the complete package process/resource ledger.

The legacy resource ledger's totals, capExceeded, and disposition rederive only its three durable produce-attempt rows and their resource-refusal dispositions. Its packageProcessHoursMaximum value is policy metadata, not evidence that this legacy ledger accounts for the package. Complete eight-packet process/storage authority, including supplemental A-P, publication, aggregate control/producer/check-caller timing and every selected/unselected retained execution exactly once, belongs exclusively to verification-v2 packageProcessAccounting/packageResourceAccounting and may veto the pre-verification aggregate candidates.

Every callerInvocationResults row uses the packet protocol's exact caller/evaluator/source authority. Complete rows embed a canonical evaluatorResult and exact executed/evaluated check and control rosters; child-registered-cap rows embed no evaluator verdict or check credit. The terminal candidate carries only the pre-candidate subsequence, verification carries the complete rerun roster, and terminal-v2 exact-copies it without a self-identity.

execution follows the packet verification.executionProvenanceRule. It is non-null only when the selected normal credit-bearing route has an exact completed main evaluator interval. It is null for every structurally verified radial artifact/prelaunch/registered-cap refusal because zero-worker, production-cap, and child-cap routes have no truthful completed numerical-evaluator interval; callerInvocationResults and governedTiming retain the independently rederived structural/cap provenance. Other maker-return routes publish no verification-v2.

A produce verification reopens its attempt-v2 ledger, selects the exact sole materializable row, and copies no timing claim: invocationRecords, governedInvocationElapsedNanoseconds, governedInvocationWallSeconds, and processHours must exactly rederive from that row.

A supplemental-A-P, publish, or aggregate verification records the exact full protocol verificationInvocationRoster with execution-only timing states and parent-owned monotonic elapsed-nanosecond intervals; UTC instants are provenance only.

selectedPacketIds is the exact catalogue execution-order prefix ending at this packet. priorPacketVerifications contains every earlier member exactly once and excludes the current receipt so the schema has no self-hash cycle.

An attempt row contributes through a selected packet verification or unselectedAttemptRows, never both. The exact union covers every governed execution once; duplicateAccountingVerdict and omissionAccountingVerdict must both pass.
At aggregate, selectedPacketIds contains all eight packets in catalogue order and priorPacketVerifications contains the preceding seven exact manifest-pinned verification identities.

A moving/static or nonproduce maker-return carries no successful packet verification and therefore ends the current v1 catalogue prefix before aggregate. Any separately frozen successor protocol must reopen and count that terminal timing and retained raw root exactly once before authorizing another attempt; current v1 never claims it through unselectedAttemptRows.

totalElapsedNanoseconds equals the exact integer prior-selected, unselected-attempt, and current elapsed-nanosecond sum. totalProcessHours is derived once by division by 3600000000000; equality to 86400000000000 nanoseconds (24 hours) is allowed and one nanosecond greater refuses.

Produce packetResourceAccounting reopens the selected attempt-v2 resourceRecord. Nonproduce accounting independently censuses the append-only terminal attempt root; terminal retained bytes therefore equal the observed high-water.

Materialized publication artifacts are exact identities. The current verification and later terminal receipt use only their two exact protocol-registered path/byte projections, avoiding self-reference; the next packet replaces both with manifest-pinned exact identities.

packageResourceAccounting uses the same exact catalogue prefix as packageProcessAccounting, counts the 1,629,577-byte physical-copy baseline once, and covers every selected packet raw/published copy exactly once. Aggregate covers all eight packets; S9 rechecks the final committed actual bytes.

Moving publication deterministically emits resultId c0v-moving-result-v1 and static emits c0v-static-result-v1; both have terminalStatus and scientificDisposition refusal, null witness/evaluation, negativeControlDisposition not-run-no-credit, and resourceDisposition within-cap. Each layer artifact-index-v1 has bundleId phase10-numerical-verification-v1, excludes its own identity, and is sorted by output ID and path over the exact science protocol, reference/refusal, attempt ledger, and result; radial adds witness and evaluation exactly for production-complete and forbids both on validated refusal.
